landmarks.name: Mount Yasur
landmarks.writeup: An active volcano on Tanna Island, known for its frequent eruptions and accessible lava lake.

wiki.extract: Mount Yasur is an active volcano on Tanna Island, Vanuatu, 361 m (1,184 ft) high above sea level, on the coast near Sulphur Bay, northeast of the taller Mount Tukosmera, which was active in the Pleistocene. It has a largely unvegetated pyroclastic cone with a nearly circular summit crater 400 m in diameter.

landmarks.name: Mele Cascades
landmarks.writeup: A series of beautiful waterfalls near Port Vila, popular for swimming and hiking.

wiki.extract: Efate, originally named Sandwich Island and also known as Île Vate or just Vate, is an island in the Pacific Ocean. It is part of the Shefa Province in Vanuatu, and the capital city, Port Vila, is located on the island.

landmarks.name: Chief Roi Mata's Domain
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site encompassing archaeological sites related to a powerful 16th-century chief.

wiki.extract: Roi Mata was a chiefly title in the central islands of Vanuatu. It was borne by a long dynasty of chiefs, from the 11th to the 17th century.

cultural_events.name: Naghol (Land Diving)
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional ritual on Pentecost Island where men jump from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles.

wiki.extract: Land diving is a ritual performed by the men of the southern part of Pentecost Island, Vanuatu. Men jump off wooden towers around 20 to 30 meters high, with two tree vines wrapped around the ankles. The tradition has developed into a tourist attraction. According to the Guinness World Records, the g-force experienced by those at their lowest point in the dive is the greatest experienced in the non-industrialized world by humans.

cultural_events.name: Fest'Napuan
cultural_events.writeup: An annual music and cultural festival in Port Vila celebrating Vanuatu's diverse cultures and arts.

wiki.extract: Not Drowning, Waving are a musical group formed in Melbourne, Australia, in 1983 by David Bridie and John Phillips. Their music combines elements of rock, ambient music and world music; their lyrics deal with characteristically Australian topics: word-pictures of landscapes and people, the seasons, and some political issues – such as Indonesia's invasion of East Timor. The group have released six studio albums and two soundtracks before disbanding in 1994. They have briefly reformed in 2001, 2003, 2005–2006 and 2025–present. From 2005 to 2007, they issued three compilation albums. Not Drowning, Waving won the ARIA Award for Best Independent Release at the ARIA Music Awards of 1992 for Proof, their soundtrack for the 1991 film of the same name. In 1991, Bridie and fellow members of Not Drowning, Waving, formed a side-project, My Friend the Chocolate Cake, to play more acoustic-based material. In 2025, Not Drowning, Waving again reformed, with George Telek, to produce a series of live shows and a new studio album, Malira.

food_writeup: Vanuatu cuisine features root crops like taro and yam, fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and traditional dishes such as lap lap, a baked pudding made from grated root vegetables.
brief_history: Vanuatu was first settled by Melanesian people around 3,000 years ago. It was colonized by both Britain and France in the 19th century, becoming the New Hebrides Condominium. Vanuatu gained independence in 1980.

important_people.name: Walter Lini
important_people.description: First Prime Minister and independence leader

current_conflicts: Vanuatu is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts at present.

commentary.inflation_management: The Reserve Bank of Vanuatu kept inflation low and boring for most of the period - between 0.8% and 5.3% from 2006 through 2022, with series lows of 0.8% in 2014 and 2016. That stability broke in 2023, when post-cyclone supply disruption and global prices pushed inflation to a series high of 11.2%. It collapsed back to 1.1% in 2024 and a projected 1.7% in 2025. The vatu's managed float and a conservative central bank helped, but the 2023 spike shows how a single cyclone season can undo a decade of price stability in a small import-dependent economy.
commentary.debt_management: Vanuatu was a low-debt economy - 16-20% of GDP from 2006 to 2014 - until Cyclone Pam struck in 2015. Reconstruction borrowing, including Chinese-financed infrastructure, lifted debt to 32.2% in 2015 and a series high of 46.4% in 2017. It has since stabilized around 39-43%, with a projected 40.9% in 2025, as GDP nearly tripled in dollar terms ($0.48bn to $1.32bn) and tourism recovered. The debt is sustainable at current levels, but the ratchet pattern is clear: each major cyclone permanently lifts the debt stock, and climate change is making major cyclones more frequent.

key_events.event: March: Cyclone Pam, a category 5 storm, devastated the islands and drove the debt surge.
COVID-19 border closure froze tourism, the main foreign-exchange earner.
March: twin cyclones Judy and Kevin struck within days, the costliest disaster pair in the country's history.
Political instability with successive no-confidence motions; citizenship-by-investment revenue under scrutiny.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The economy will keep growing on tourism and agriculture, but the fiscal model - borrow to rebuild after each cyclone - is only sustainable if disasters stay infrequent, which they won't. Debt is likely to ratchet higher with each major storm. Diversifying revenue (the citizenship program is politically fragile) and building genuine climate-resilient infrastructure are the tests. Donor and concessional finance will remain essential.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
